newsitem.title: USA: CyberCash upbeat on Q1 business.
newsitem.headline: CyberCash upbeat on Q1 business.

text.p: CyberCash Inc Executive Vice President Bruce Wilson said the company is following through on its strategy and has made favorable progress in boosting revenues in its first quarter.
"There's one thing on our mind and that's revenues," he said in a presentation to analysts at a Robertson Stephens technology conference here.
"The revenue is coming," he said, but declined to discuss details. "We are making excellent progress on all fronts. Our strategy is in place and being executed."

Vienna, Virginia-based CyberCash develops software and services for secure financial transactions on the Internet and last September launched a micropayment service that enables small cash transactions over the Internet.

Wilson said the company believes this service, dubbed CyberCoin, will be the company's primary source of revenue in the future and represented its "killer app" or blockbuster application for electronic commerce.
Working with financial processing institutions, such as Visa and MasterCard, CyberCash develops and implements on-line financial transactions.
Its initial service, for credit card payments, was launched in April 1995. ((sam.perry@reuters.com, Palo Alto Bureau 415 846 5400))
